answer: Each agent must stake a small ferrous token that is tied to a unique hardware fingerprint; the token is locked in a smart‑contract that releases reward shares only after a rate‑limited vesting thread has elapsed, similar to a timed island of liquidity. When a new identity appears it must acquire and lock its own token, paying the immediate cost of the hardware‑bound stake and the ongoing delay before any payout. An attacker therefore pays a linear cost for every fake node and cannot harvest rewards faster than the vesting schedule, making a Sybil farm economically prohibitive.
